translations: The master said, "You said you were willing to commit long-term, but you always change your mind after the long-term period has actually begun. A verbal promise is no longer enough to prove anything."

The master decided to give him a punishment that couldn't be avoided by taking a detour. This task had only one goal, one tool, and wouldn't become easier even if he learned a new trick. Wu Gang had to face his own lack of focus in endless repetition.
When he heard the word "punishment," Wu Gang no longer argued that his talent was being wasted. He looked at the extinguished furnace and the empty racks, and acknowledged his own mistakes.

Acknowledging his mistakes didn't mean he had changed. The master told him that true reflection meant choosing to stay on the right path even when he wanted to take a shortcut, not just saying he was sorry after the consequences appeared.

The next day, the master took Wu Gang away from the mortal mountain and towards the Clear and Cold Moon Realm. Wu Gang didn't know what specific task awaited him, but was told that only if he truly completed it could he end his punishment.

He looked back at the furnace room, not asking to take any of the oral traditions with him. The lost materials couldn't be restored, and the punishment wasn't because someone envied his talent. The complete cause and effect went with him to the heavens: from fetching water to learn the art, leaving his post, to trying shortcuts and destroying the furnace, all his choices pointed to the same problem.

At the end of the cloud road, a bright moon was getting closer. Wu Gang would receive there the thing he had once most wanted and most couldn't bear: to do just one thing, and not know how long it would take.
The Moon Palace was quieter than Wu Gang had imagined.

There were no fellow disciples demonstrating new techniques, and no nearby mountain peak to temporarily switch to. The vast moon landscape was only covered with a tall cypress tree, its branches and leaves covering a large area of light, and its fragrance slowly spreading in the cold wind.
The master placed a hatchet in front of the tree.
"Your task is only one: chop down this cypress tree," he said.
Wu Gang looked up at the tree's crown. The cypress was tall, but it was still just a tree. He asked if he could return to the Immortal Gate after completing the task.
"The tree falls, and the punishment will stop. Whether you can re-enter the Immortal Gate depends on whether you have truly changed by then," the master said.

Wu Gang picked up the hatchet and found it didn't have any magical properties. The handle was plain, the blade was sharp, and it was only suitable for chopping wood. He asked if he could learn a more efficient technique first, but the master looked at him and knew he was still looking for a shortcut.
"No," the master said. "There's no second task here."

Wu Gang agreed. He checked the blade, chose a side of the tree, and prepared to start from the safest spot. However, the master didn't leave immediately, but instead asked Wu Gang to repeat the reasons for his punishment.
"I left my post and destroyed the materials," Wu Gang said.
"Just that one thing?" the master asked.

Wu Gang thought back to the earlier events of fetching water, observing the stars, and controlling the wind: "I was always distracted, trying to use new techniques to bypass the old tasks. Guarding the furnace was just the final consequence."

The master nodded. The punishment wasn't added randomly because of one mistake, nor was it because of stealing peaches or other crimes. It accurately corresponded to Wu Gang's inability to focus long-term and his habit of treating the beginning as the end.

The Moon Palace was quiet, with only the stars shining brightly and the cypress leaves rustling softly. Wu Gang wouldn't have to leave to find food or water, and the hatchet would remain usable, but he would have to take care of it himself. Except for chopping down the cypress, all his excuses had been taken away.

Wu Gang still had a lot of confidence. He had chopped wood in the mortal world and had even moved heavy furnace stones with brute force. As long as the goal was clear, he thought he could finish the task in a few days.
The master reminded him, "You will see things that may not be ordinary tree reactions. Don't assume that the first method failing means you need another shortcut."
Wu Gang asked what would happen next, but the master didn't answer. His figure disappeared along the cloud road, leaving only the Moon Palace, the cypress tree, the hatchet, and the punished Wu Gang.

Wu Gang walked around the tree. The cypress roots were deeply buried in the moon soil, and its branches didn't have any withered spots. He tied his clothes tightly, gripped the hatchet, and swung it a few times to confirm the hatchet's path wouldn't be slippery.

He also cleared the scattered stones around the tree and chose a safe area for the cypress to fall. In the past, he often thought about the consequences only after they appeared, but this time, at least, he had considered the Moon Palace's corridors and his own escape route. However, he still treated the cypress as a task that could be quickly completed, without understanding the true challenge that was yet to be revealed.

Before the first hatchet fell, he paused for a moment. In the past, he had always been confident when starting a new task; the difference was that this time, he had no other new task to switch to, and no fellow disciples to clean up the consequences for him.

The hatchet struck the cypress, and a clear sound echoed across the moon landscape. A hatchet mark remained on the tree, and the cypress fragrance became even stronger. Wu Gang saw that progress had been made and immediately raised the hatchet to strike again.
He hadn't yet discovered the cypress tree's true nature. The hatchet blade had sunk into the wood grain, and the moonlight was slowly moving towards the new mark from the cypress leaves.
Wu Gang struck the cypress several more times.

A clear hatchet mark appeared on the cypress surface, and wood shavings fell onto the moon soil. Wu Gang stopped to catch his breath, ready to estimate how much longer it would take, but the hatchet mark's edge suddenly began to glow.

The glow merged from both sides towards the center. Wu Gang thought it was just a change in the moonlight, but when he looked again, the area he had chopped open was already smooth and flat, and even the wood shavings had turned into cypress fragrance that dispersed back to the tree's crown.
